slides.title: Networking concepts
slides.sub: Domain 1: the foundation for everything else
slides.say: Welcome to domain one of the Network Plus N10-009 exam: networking concepts. It is worth twenty-three percent of the exam and it is the foundation for every other domain. We will move quickly through the O S I model, appliances, cloud, ports and protocols, cabling, topologies, I P v four addressing, and modern network designs.

slides.title: 1.1 The OSI model
head: Layer
Job
Examples
rows: Set up, manage, and end sessions
slides.say: The O S I model has seven layers. Layer seven, application, provides network services to programs. Six, presentation, formats, encrypts, and compresses data. Five, session, sets up, manages, and ends sessions. Four, transport, handles end-to-end delivery and ports, with T C P and U D P. Three, network, handles logical addressing and routing, which is where I P and routers live. Two, data link, uses frames and mac addresses, which is where switches live. And one, physical, moves bits across the medium. A classic memory aid is: Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away, from layer one up.

slides.title: 1.2 Appliances
head: Device
What it does
rows: Filters traffic with rules; stateful tracks sessions
Detects attacks / detects and blocks them inline
Stands in for clients or servers; can filter content
Connects wireless clients to the wired network
slides.say: Objective one point two covers appliances. A router forwards packets between networks at layer three. A switch forwards frames by mac address at layer two, and a layer three switch can also route between V LANs. A firewall filters traffic with rules, and a stateful firewall tracks sessions. An I D S detects attacks, while an I P S sits in line and blocks them. A load balancer spreads requests across servers, a proxy stands in for clients or servers and can filter content, and an access point connects wireless clients to the wired network.

slides.title: 1.3 Cloud concepts
items: Public, private, hybrid, and community deployment models
IaaS, PaaS, SaaS: you manage less at each step
VPC: your own isolated network inside a public cloud
Connectivity: VPN over the internet, or a private direct connection
Security groups and network ACLs control cloud traffic
NFV runs network functions as software
slides.say: For cloud, know the deployment models: public, private, hybrid, and community. Know the service models, I a a S, pass, and sass. You manage less at each step, with I a a S giving you the most control and sass the least. A V P C is your own isolated network inside a public cloud. You connect to it with a V P N over the internet, or with a private direct connection that avoids the internet. Security groups and network A C Ls control traffic in the cloud, and network functions virtualization runs network functions as software.

slides.title: 1.4 Ports you must know
head: Port
Protocol
Port
Protocol
slides.say: Objective one point four is ports and protocols, and the exam expects you to know them cold. F T P uses twenty and twenty-one. S S H and S F T P use twenty-two. Telnet is twenty-three. S M T P is twenty-five. D N S is fifty-three. D H C P uses sixty-seven and sixty-eight. T F T P is sixty-nine. H T T P is eighty and H T T P S is four forty-three. P O P three is one-ten and I map is one forty-three. N T P is one twenty-three. S N M P uses one sixty-one for polling and one sixty-two for traps. L D A P is three eighty-nine and L D A P S is six thirty-six. S M B is four forty-five, syslog is five fourteen, and R D P is thirty-three eighty-nine.

slides.title: 1.4 Traffic types and TCP vs UDP
items: Unicast: one sender to one receiver
Multicast: one sender to a group
Broadcast: one sender to everyone on the segment
Anycast: one address, the nearest server answers
TCP: connection-oriented, reliable, handshake
UDP: connectionless, fast, no delivery guarantee
slides.say: Know the traffic types. Unicast goes from one sender to one receiver. Multicast goes to a group. Broadcast goes to everyone on the segment. And anycast uses one address that is shared by several servers, and the nearest one answers. T C P is connection-oriented and reliable, and it uses a three-way handshake. U D P is connectionless and fast, but it does not guarantee delivery, which suits voice, video, and D N S queries.

slides.title: 1.5 Media and transceivers
head: Type
Key facts
rows: Short copper link inside a rack
slides.say: For cabling, Cat five E carries one gigabit over one hundred meters. Cat six carries ten gigabits up to fifty-five meters, and Cat six A carries ten gigabits over the full one hundred meters. Multimode fiber is used over shorter distances with cheaper optics, and single-mode fiber reaches the longest distances, measured in kilometers. Transceivers plug into switches: S F P is one gigabit, S F P plus is ten gigabits, and Q S F P is forty. A D A C or Twinax cable is a short copper link, typically inside a rack.

slides.title: 1.6 Topologies and architectures
items: Star: every device connects to a central switch
Full mesh: every node connects to every other; partial mesh: some
Hub and spoke: branches connect to a central site
Three-tier: core, distribution, access
Collapsed core: core and distribution combined
Spine and leaf: data center design; east-west traffic is server to server
slides.say: Topologies. In a star, every device connects to a central switch. In a mesh, nodes connect to each other, fully or partially, which gives redundancy. Hub and spoke connects branches to a central site. For campus designs, know the three-tier model: core, distribution, and access, and the collapsed core, which combines the first two. Data centers use spine and leaf, where every leaf switch connects to every spine. There, traffic between servers is called east-west, and traffic in and out of the data center is north-south.

slides.title: 1.7 IPv4 addressing
head: Range
Meaning
slides.say: Now I P v four addressing. The private ranges are ten dot zero slash eight, one seventy-two dot sixteen slash twelve, and one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight slash sixteen. The range one sixty-nine dot two fifty-four is A P I P A, which a host uses when it cannot reach D H C P. One twenty-seven dot zero dot zero dot one is loopback. For subnetting, usable hosts equal two to the power of the host bits, minus two. A slash twenty-four has two hundred fifty-four hosts. A slash twenty-six has sixty-two hosts, with the mask two fifty-five dot two fifty-five dot two fifty-five dot one ninety-two. Practice these until they are automatic.

slides.title: 1.8 Modern network designs
items: SDN: separate the control plane from the data plane
SD-WAN: manage WAN links centrally with policy
VXLAN: Layer 2 over a Layer 3 network
Zero trust: verify every request, never trust by location
SASE: network and security delivered from the cloud
Infrastructure as code: configure devices from versioned files
IPv6: 128-bit; dual stack, tunneling, or NAT64 for transition
slides.say: Finally, modern designs. Software-defined networking separates the control plane from the data plane, so a controller decides and devices forward. S D wan manages wide area links centrally with policy. V X LAN carries layer two traffic over a layer three network. Zero trust means verify every request and never trust by location. Sassy delivers network and security services from the cloud. Infrastructure as code configures devices from versioned files. And I P version six uses one hundred twenty-eight bit addresses, with dual stack, tunneling, or nat sixty-four to transition from I P version four.

slides.title: Domain 1 recap
items: Know all seven OSI layers and what lives at each
Memorize the port list, including secure versions
Match cable and transceiver to speed and distance
Know three-tier and spine-and-leaf traffic patterns
Subnet quickly: hosts equal 2^n minus 2
slides.say: To recap domain one: know all seven layers and what lives at each. Memorize the port list, including the secure versions. Match cable and transceiver type to speed and distance. Know the three-tier and spine-and-leaf designs. And be able to subnet quickly. Good luck.
